correctness.rationale: The equation is q(y)=h_c(x)=x(c-p(x)) over C*, with exactly m simple nonzero zeros. A singular point of the total hypersurface would have y=0 and h_c'=0 at such a zero, impossible. The regular quadric A retracts to S^(n-2) by writing its points as a+ib and shrinking b while maintaining a perpendicular and adjusting its norm. To justify the global reduction in Step 4 without properness, take disjoint closed simple-zero disks D_j defined by the coordinate h_c, with distinct attachment points on their boundaries. The rest of C* retracts, fixing the boundary circles of these disks, to a graph of those circles and an origin circle joined by a tree of stems: first trim the two annular ends, then cut the resulting planar surface along stems and retract onto its inner boundary circles and the joining tree. This base homotopy H_t lifts over the regular region by multiplying y by the continuous square root of h_c(H_t(x))/h_c(x) starting at 1. The lift fixes the disk boundaries, so extends by the identity on the disk pieces. Each inverse image of D_j is the contractible set |q(y)|<=epsilon, by radial contraction of y. Since the boundary loop over each D_j is already in that disk piece, its stem contributes only a cylinder over A connecting the disk piece to the regular graph. Contracting the tree and using the mapping-cylinder pushouts leaves the origin mapping torus with m cones on its fibers, all inclusions homotopic by transport. Collapsing the first fiber gives the suspension of A with its two poles identified, homotopy equivalent to S^1 wedge Sigma A. The later cone maps are nullhomotopic and each wedges on Sigma A. This proves the full bouquet, including n=3, where A retracts to S^1; connectedness and the claimed integral groups follow. The Euler characteristic and the frozen verification checklist are not used to infer homotopy type.

evidence: Write the rational function as (q+xp(x))/x. Takeuchi distinguishes generic cohomology from predicted homotopy. The local handle principle provides a vanishing cycle over a simple zero, but not the effect of the puncture or the nonproper exterior by itself.

evidence: The equation is an affine quadratic suspension with the full x=0 fiber deleted. In n=3 it is uv=h_c(x) in C* x C^2 via u=y_1+i y_2 and v=y_1-i y_2. Alternatively dividing one variable by x converts it to uv=c-p(x) over C*.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Affine-surface statements over the entire coordinate line do not automatically identify this complement. Dubouloz describes additive actions and affine-line fibrations of whole surfaces; Seidel studies suspensions and Lefschetz-fibration categories, not the punctured-base homotopy type.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge pass for the explicit integral homotopy and sphere count on the stated fibers, not for the general bouquet conjecture or for the classical local quadratic model. Takeuchi predicts a bouquet under his general assumptions but proves cohomological conclusions; the closest affine-suspension and handle results inspected do not establish the deleted-fiber nonproper case together with its attaching maps. The indexed search found no materially matching distinct finding.
residual_risks: Broader nonproper Lefschetz or suspension-complement literature, especially for affine surfaces, could contain an equivalent result.
This is not a claim about the exact scope of Takeuchi's genericity conditions or about absolute priority.

value.rationale: This gives a full integral homotopy computation in an infinite natural class with nontrivial fundamental group, including control of how singular pieces interact with regular monodromy. It supplies concrete evidence for the rational-fiber bouquet picture and supplies sphere counts for every indicated level, beyond an Euler characteristic or a list of Betti numbers.
